title: Assessing Canopy Structure of Soybean Plants
author: Isla Causon
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.rmsd46e

steps.title: Locate soybean line and rows
steps.instruction: Use the field map to identify the target soybean line (each line has 4 rows). Note that there are always 5 adjacent soybean lines separated by buffer zones containing two rows of generic soybean. The lines follow an ascending‑number weaving pattern, so the next soybean line is directly next to the previous one.

steps.title: Select sampling rows and plants
steps.instruction: Sample leaves only from the 2nd and 3rd rows (the middle rows) of the chosen line, leaving the 1st and 4th rows as buffers. Choose three representative plants within the line—neither too small nor too large—and record their identifiers on a data sheet or spreadsheet.

steps.title: Record overall plant height
steps.instruction: For each selected plant, measure the vertical distance from the soil surface (bottom of the stem) to the bottom of the topmost flower bud (top) and note the value in centimeters.

steps.title: Measure internodes and secondary stems
steps.instruction: Starting at the ground, measure each internode length in centimeters, proceeding upward until the bottom of the top flower bud is reached. For the first internode, measure from the ground to the beginning of the internode; for subsequent internodes, measure from the base of the previous internode to the base of the next. At each internode, check for secondary stems (branches off the main stem). If present, measure the secondary‑stem length from the main stem to the base of its terminal leaf (cm) and count the number of tertiary stems (petioles) emerging from that secondary stem.

substeps.instruction: Measure first internode from ground to its start.
Measure each subsequent internode from the previous internode base to the next.
If a secondary stem is present at an internode, measure its length (cm).
Count tertiary stems (petioles) on each secondary stem.

steps.title: Divide canopy into thirds and measure leaves
steps.instruction: Divide the total plant height by three to define three canopy levels: lower, middle, and upper thirds. In each canopy level, select four representative leaves and measure both leaf length and leaf width in centimeters. This yields two measurements for twelve leaves per plant. If a leaf belongs to the middle canopy layer but its secondary stem attaches in the lower canopy, count the leaf as middle canopy.

steps.title: Measure secondary‑stem angles
steps.instruction: Using a protractor, measure the angle between each secondary stem and the vertical (90° from the ground). Assign a grade according to the following system: grade 2 or 1 for acute angles (< 90°), grade 0 for exactly 90°, grade ‑1 or ‑2 for obtuse angles (> 90°). If the measured angle falls between two grades (dotted lines), record a grade of 0.5.
